description: CT-RATE is a public open-source dataset of non-contrast 3D chest CT volumes paired with corresponding radiology text reports. It contains 25,692 scans from 21,304 unique patients, totaling 50,188 reconstructed volumes, and includes anonymized metadata and automatically extracted global abnormality labels.
name: CT-RATE
rai:annotatorDemographics: Radiology reports were originally authored by radiologists. For translation review and de-identification, bilingual final-year medical students reviewed and corrected all translated reports and removed residual personal information.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The automated report labeler was evaluated on a held-out validation set, with Supplementary Table 2 reporting precision, recall, and F1 scores for each of 18 abnormalities; the paper states these results show robust classification across abnormalities, ensuring the dataset is enriched with high-quality labels.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For label extraction, the authors manually annotated 1,000 reports after merging findings and impression sections to identify 18 abnormalities. Conditions not referenced in either section were considered absent, and similar conditions were grouped under shared categories such as lung opacity and lung nodules. The annotated reports were split into 800 training and 200 validation reports to fine-tune an automated report labeler, which was then applied to the remaining reports.
rai:dataBiases: The authors explicitly note that biases inherent to their single-institution dataset may influence self-supervised training, because the data originate from a single geographic and clinical setting, which may limit generalizability to other populations. They also note dependence on report terminology and prompt choice, as variability in how diseases are described across reports can affect zero-shot detection accuracy.
rai:dataCollection: The dataset was curated from chest CT volumes and corresponding radiology text reports from Istanbul Medipol University Mega Hospital. The authors incorporated every reconstructed non-contrast chest CT volume from the hospital database, anonymized reports, metadata, and volumes, translated reports from Turkish to English using Google Translate API with bilingual medical-student review, and excluded contrast studies or scans involving body parts other than the chest.
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The paper notes that the external UPMC validation dataset lacks publicly available detailed metadata and that RAD-ChestCT lacks a Mosaic attenuation label and text reports, but for CT-RATE itself no explicit missing-data problem is described.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data consist of non-contrast chest CT volumes, associated radiology reports, and metadata from the hospital database. Reports originally contained four sections—clinical information, technique, findings, and impression—and the dataset contains the original raw CT data.
rai:dataImputationProtocol: For reports with content of fewer than 512 tokens, the text encoder uses padding with the <PAD> token, and padded tokens are masked during the attention mechanism.
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is limited by being collected from a single institution and a single geographic and clinical setting, which may reduce generalizability. Current coverage is limited to chest CT volumes, and the paper notes future work should extend to other 3D modalities and anatomical regions. The paper also notes that high-quality 3D benchmarks and broader multi-institutional data are still lacking.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The dataset includes automatically extracted global abnormality labels for 18 abnormalities by fine-tuning a report classifier on 1,000 manually annotated reports and applying it to the remaining reports. The dataset also includes organ-level anatomical segmentation labels generated using a state-of-the-art segmentation model. For model training use, reports' findings and impression sections were merged for annotation, and CT volumes were standardized by resizing, cropping, and padding.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Reports were anonymized by removing personal information with targeted regular-expression searches, translated from Turkish to English using the Google Translate API, then reviewed and corrected by bilingual final-year medical students. CT volumes were filtered to exclude contrast material and non-chest studies, standardized for orientation, anonymized in metadata, resized to uniform spacing of 0.75 mm × 0.75 mm × 1.5 mm, center-cropped or padded to 480×480×240, converted to Hounsfield Units using intercept and slope metadata, clipped to -1000 to 1000 HU, and normalized to -1 to 1 during training.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is presented as enabling future innovations in medical AI, reducing radiologists’ workload, improving diagnostic support, and potentially improving patient care. The paper also frames the resource as supporting educational and clinical research use through open access and a user-friendly interface.
rai:dataUseCases: Intended uses include contrastive language-image pretraining for 3D chest CT, zero-shot multi-abnormality detection, finetuning for abnormality classification, CT volume retrieval, report-to-volume retrieval, visual question answering, radiology report generation, visual grounding, and anatomical localization.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Google Translate API was used to translate reports from Turkish to English; a finetuned RadBERT-RoBERTa-4m automated text classifier was used to extract 18 abnormality labels from reports; organ-level anatomical segmentation labels were generated using a state-of-the-art segmentation model; TotalSegmentator was used to extract pulmonary-nodule structured metadata for downstream CT-CHAT development.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The source data include patient medical images, radiology reports, patient age, patient sex, symptoms and medical history in report sections, and metadata fields such as StudyDate before anonymization. The paper states that all personal information pertaining to patients and medical professionals was removed before release.
